The '''Rebel Honor Guard''' was the ceremonial guard of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. It comprised former [[Senate Guard/Legends|Blue Guards]] of the defunct [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic's]] [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]], and several survivors of the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. 

==Organization==
The [[Guerrilla warfare/Legends|guerrilla]] nature of the Rebel Alliance minimizes the use of ceremonial uniforms and personnel. However, there are occasions when pomp and formality are either required by protocol or desired by Alliance leaders and soldiers alike: medal ceremonies, formal visits to high-ranking officials, and bereavement traditions, to name a few.<ref name=":0">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

To fulfill these roles, the Alliance maintains a small ceremonial unit known as the Rebel Honor Guard. Trained as bodyguards, they serve as protectors of the Alliance leadership during formal occasions. Though they are not trained to the same level of ability or fanaticism as the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Royal Guard]], Rebel Honor Guards are professional, disciplined, and loyal.<ref name=":0" />

Honor Guard personnel are regularly rotated back into standard Rebel units. There, they share their training with other unit members, which increases the likelihood that a few Honor Guards are present in any given sector. However, the primary reason for this rotation is [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma's]] awareness of the dangers of keeping an elite unit too close to Alliance leadership. By rotating the troops, she aims to prevent the Honor Guards from becoming overly loyal to any single leader or developing a sense of elitism. <ref name=":0" />

==History==
The Rebel Honor Guard served as the ceremonial guard of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]&mdash;better known as the Rebel Alliance&mdash;a resistance movement opposed to [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Initially, many Honor Guards had been former members of the [[Senate Guard/Legends|Blue Guard]],<ref name="Mini">{{SWMiniCite|set=Legacy of the Force|pack=Rebel Honor Guard}}</ref> the duty of which was to protect the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] and the [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] in the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]].<ref name="Senate Guard">{{DB|organization|senateguard|Senate Guard}}</ref> When the then Chancellor Palpatine turned the Republic into his Galactic Empire, some of the Blue Guards refused to join the new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] red-clad [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]].<ref name="Mini" /> They may have had relations with the [[Alliance Elite Guard]], who were tasked with nearly the same duties.

Following the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] by the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]<ref name="Honor Guard">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|pack=#10: Rebel Honor Guard (Yavin)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tac10rebguard.asp}}</ref> in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the Rebel Honor Guard comprised survivors from that once ceremonious planet. While many Rebel officers lacked proper dress [[uniform]]s, the survivors of Alderaan had retained theirs, thereby conferring the Honor Guard a more solemn aura.<ref name="Honor Guard" />

Shortly after that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]], a group of Alliance [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] attacked and [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] the Death Star over the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]]. In celebration of their victory, the Rebels held an [[Royal Award Ceremony/Legends|award ceremony]] in the [[Grand Audience Chamber|Throne Room]] of the [[Great Temple/Legends|Massassi Station]]&mdash;an ancient temple located on the [[Yavin 4/Legends|fourth]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of Yavin.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The members of the Honor Guards who were [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] survivors were selected to stand in front of the Throne Room's main doors during the ceremony, which honored [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] for their efforts in destroying the Death Star.<ref name="Honor Guard" />

After the Alliance finally got the upper hand against the Empire and evolved into a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Rebel Honor Guards were reorganized into the [[New Republic Honor Guard]].<ref name="JS">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref>

==Equipment==
The Rebel Honor Guards wore dark [[Color/Legends|green]], button down jackets with pockets, matching pants and black [[Boot/Legends|boots]]. They wore [[Armor/Legends|helmets]] similar to that of the [[Rebel Vanguard/Legends|Rebel Vanguard]] troopers and wielded an [[Electropole/Legends|electropole]].<ref name="Honor Guard" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Rebel Honor Guards first appeared during the ending segment of the [[1977]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga. An action figure of the Rebel Honor Guard was released by the [[Hasbro]] toy company in [[2007]], as part of their ''[[Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection]]'' set. The background of all the Honor Guard sentries present during the award ceremony was expanded on the action figure's accompanying card. In [[2008]], a 34 mm scale model of the Rebel Honor Guard was released for the ''[[Star Wars Miniatures]]'', an [[Roleplaying game|RPG]]-style game by [[Wizards of the Coast]].

===Inconsistencies===
The Honor Guards sentries did appear in the [[1987]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Droids (1986) 8|''Droids'' (1986) 8]], although with a significantly different uniform than what was shown in ''A New Hope''. The sentries' design in ''According to the Droids'' was likely based on a piece of early concept art drawn by [[John Mollo]] for the movie. That conceptual drawing was later published in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]]''.
